proposed_from.topic: K1 prove recorded-propensity IPW–SVD has normalized maximum-row loss O_P(a^{loose}_{nm}) on the frozen predictable effect-only low-rank class, and prove by a same-class endogenous-target construction that uniform O_P(b_{nm}) attainment by this estimator is false. K2 prove the same-loss observed-data minimax bracket c b_{nm} ≤ R*_{nm} ≤ C(1 ∧ a^{loose}_{nm}), leaving the rate between these endpoints open. K3 prove blind causal loss and observed blind-versus-recorded disagreement resolve total drift only up to O_P(d_{nm}), retain the 0.25/0.75 Markov failure witness, and make no b_{nm}-scale iff claim. K4 retain direct finite-sample simultaneous bands with the separate sqrt(log |G_n|) multiplicity cost and no multiplier-exactness claim.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: Mehrotra et al. already provide the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale for armwise row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignment, so that scale alone is not claimed as new. No located result gives the calibrated normalized maximum-row effect-subspace frontier under a recorded history-predictable unit-by-time mask, with only the effect matrix constrained to be low rank, together with a matching converse over observed-data-measurable estimators. Nor does a located result give the blind iff frontier whose latent total drift is recoverable to \(O_P(b_{nm})\) from observed disagreement between blind and recorded fits. Athey et al. and Sun et al. supply outcome-completion Frobenius results whose assumptions and conclusions do not imply this frontier in either direction; the wider audit of Bai and Ng, Agarwal et al., Choi and Yuan, Mao et al., and Wang et al. reaches the same target-and-experiment separation. Dwivedi et al.'s closest adaptive pooled result is formally non-representable in either direction. The Markov law is a boundary example for the new row-fraction SVD, not a claimed failure of prior normalization practice. No located matrix result combines this predictable effect-subspace frontier with a growing dense causal-query family while keeping query entropy separate from row recovery.

seed_details.seed: Joint predictable-mask IPW-SVD rate, blind-drift equivalence, and simultaneous-query frontier
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:1910.04267, Introduction; Theorem 1; minimax Theorem 2; proof sections on leave-one-out and Fano; Discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper's central construction diagonal-deletes a Gram matrix and uses leave-one-out and leave-two-out sequences whose independence comes from Bernoulli entry sampling. Its minimax proof packs rank-one left factors and conditions Gaussian likelihoods on independent masks. The Discussion names general sampling patterns and uncertainty quantification as open directions.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace independent row deletion by a filtration-preserving martingale compensator, then propagate its predictable quadratic variation through the rowwise singular-space expansion.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for predictable-mask rowwise SVD, adaptive matrix completion with martingale maximum-row loss, and simultaneous adaptive low-rank bootstrap found active-sampling algorithms and scalar adaptive inference, but no theorem for this target-method pair.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from Cai et al. plus matrix Freedman because IPW errors are conditionally centered.
seed_details.rebuttal: Matrix Freedman controls the operator norm only, while Cai et al.'s first row-deletion step uses independence that fails when deleting a row changes later propensities; the blind ratio and growing-query remainder are additional nonlinear objects.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposal does not quote \(b_{nm}\) as Cai et al.'s rate, does not hide query entropy in it, and makes the adaptive denominator and sharp constant explicitly open.
seed_details.burned_reason: The sole predictable-mask angle was maximized through seven D0 solve rounds, an endogenous-target counterexample, a deterministic sine-frame hybrid, and anchor audits; the remaining minimax gap has no concrete same-assumption construction.

seed_details.seed: Blind row normalization as an exact propensity-drift divergence frontier
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2106.07695, Sections 1--3; fixed-point construction; asymptotic normality theorem; Discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper defines an affine random denominator, derives the optimal normalization through numerator-denominator covariance, and proves its limit by an independent-vector central limit theorem and delta method. Its Discussion explicitly identifies dependent observation indicators as a next problem.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the independent delta method by a rowwise martingale ratio expansion and identify the singular-space pseudo-target generated by the predictable propensity path.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for dependent-indicator adaptive normalization and predictable Hájek matrix completion returned survey and scalar normalization results, not a low-rank necessary-and-sufficient drift boundary.
seed_details.referee_objection: The iff statement is a triangle inequality after defining drift as the distance between targets.
seed_details.rebuttal: The substantive theorem is the uniform \(O_P(b_{nm})\) concentration of the same-path ratio SVD around the explicit pseudo-target; without that martingale ratio expansion the triangle bounds are unavailable and the pseudo-target itself is not known.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The drift is a law-level functional, not an assumed estimator rate, and necessity is required on a nondegenerate Markov family.

seed_details.seed: Multiplier Gaussian approximation for polynomially many dense adaptive low-rank contrasts
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:1909.00116, Introduction; four-step debiasing construction; fixed-linear-form normal approximation theorem; feasible confidence-interval theorem; concluding discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The estimator splits the sample, debiases an initial completion, projects onto estimated singular spaces, and proves a quantitative Gaussian approximation for one fixed loading. The paper notes that nonuniform sampling requires propensity calibration and does not treat a growing predictable family.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Make the tangent representation uniform over a polynomial dictionary before applying a high-dimensional martingale coupling and feasible multiplier covariance estimate.
seed_details.destination_search: Belloni and Oliveira cover martingale maxima without spectral remainders; Ma et al. bootstrap modeled-missingness coefficient coordinates rather than dense low-rank causal forms; no closer subsuming theorem was found.
seed_details.referee_objection: Belloni and Oliveira already give the required multiplier theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem begins after a martingale vector is available; the new work is the uniform leave-one-row spectral linearization and feasible covariance under predictable low-rank scores.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The pointwise benchmark and family entropy are separate formal objects, and the claim is a limit-law seed rather than another minimax seed.

seed_details.seed: Semiparametric efficiency bound for one dense contrast under a predictable low-rank experiment
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2212.11385, Introduction; online doubly-debiased construction; fixed-linear-form central limit theorem; proof via martingale increments.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper constructs an online inverse-propensity debiasing step and derives a fixed-linear-form limit after tangent projection, but its target is a matrix-contextual-bandit coefficient and it does not derive a semiparametric efficiency bound.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Specify the tangent space of the sequential low-rank law and project the pathwise score before comparing the resulting bound with tangent-debiased IPW-SVD.
seed_details.destination_search: The exact sequential experiment is not dominated by a common likelihood without further outcome-model choices, so a model-invariant efficiency bound could not be stated on the current substrate.
seed_details.referee_objection: The proposed bound is either Han et al.'s variance formula or depends on an arbitrarily chosen semiparametric model.
seed_details.rebuttal: A distinct bound may exist, but the present gaps file does not fix enough likelihood structure to defend it without changing the model.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because the efficiency model would be author-created and could make the comparison a stand-in.

seed_details.seed: Low-rank adaptive policy learning with a rowwise nuisance-regret frontier
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2106.07695, Introduction and policy-learning application in Section 4; Discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper carries adaptive normalization into a policy-learning objective under independent indicators, but its theorems concern consistent score improvement rather than a low-rank welfare-regret frontier.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Translate rowwise low-rank estimation error into policy disagreement under a margin condition, then match it by a policy-class packing under constant propensities.
seed_details.destination_search: Adaptive policy-evaluation and contextual-bandit papers occupy nearby terrain, but the required policy class and welfare functional are not specified by the brief.
seed_details.referee_objection: This changes the target from matrix recovery to a generic plug-in policy regret problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The low-rank rowwise frontier could matter for policies, but without a named policy class the seed is less direct than the fixed-estimand kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because choosing a policy would introduce a new decision problem rather than resolve the recorded mask boundary.

seed_details.seed: Path-conditional conformal inversion for adaptive low-rank counterfactual profiles
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:1909.00116, Introduction; inference construction; concluding discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The anchor derives Wald inference from independent random sampling and contains no permutation or exchangeability orbit for an adaptive assignment path.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Condition on the realized predictable design and seek a nondegenerate assignment-preserving symmetry orbit for rowwise residual scores.
seed_details.destination_search: No exact target-method match was found, and conditioning on the full adaptive history generally leaves a singleton assignment orbit, destroying finite-sample conformal content.
seed_details.referee_objection: Adaptive assignment destroys the exchangeability needed for exact conformal coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: No defensible nondegenerate symmetry was found under the current assumptions, so the objection holds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped rather than assuming exchangeability that the predictable design does not provide.

seed_details.seed: Explicit weight-map decomposition and correction of blind row SVD
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:1911.02768, Introduction; adaptively weighted AIPW estimator; arm-value central limit theorem; martingale proof; Discussion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper shows why raw adaptive IPW can have mixture-like behavior and restores a scalar martingale limit with predictable weights. Its proof constructs a martingale-difference sequence and verifies predictable variance and Lyapunov conditions.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Lift the scalar weight decomposition to the singular-space tangent map and estimate the propensity-induced pseudo-target correction.
seed_details.destination_search: Mao, Wong, and Chen estimate structured nonsequential propensities, but no adaptive matrix paper provides this explicit blind-weight map and correction.
seed_details.referee_objection: The correction is just to use the recorded IPW estimator already available.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection limits the correction's novelty; the weight-map characterization survives, but it is subsumed by the sharper iff-drift seed.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped as a separate seed because its correction collapses to the main recorded estimator.

seed_details.seed: Predictable balancing weights with a heterogeneous-mask minimax guarantee
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2106.05850, Introduction; convex balancing-weight construction; uniform Frobenius upper theorem; heterogeneous-sampling minimax lower theorem; conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper chooses weights by a spectral balancing program and proves Frobenius upper and lower bounds under independent heterogeneous Bernoulli observation. Its data-estimated weights already require careful dependence control, but the observation law is not sequential.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Make the balancing program predictable and prove that its same-path weights retain conditional centering before deriving a rowwise rather than Frobenius risk.
seed_details.destination_search: Active matrix-completion papers choose samples to reveal coherent spaces, but they optimize acquisition rather than analyze logged randomized treatment scores.
seed_details.referee_objection: When propensities are recorded, balance weights solve a harder problem than necessary and target a different missingness model.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the brief's primary setting, so this remains a fallback for unrecorded propensities rather than the selected kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped because it weakens the direct HeartSteps link and changes the estimator named in the topic.

seed_details.seed: Extreme-value limit for the full rowwise singular-vector process
seed_details.anchor_locator: arXiv:2403.14899, Introduction; iterative least-squares construction; pointwise normality theorems; multiplier simultaneous-testing theorem; Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The paper models observation probabilities through logistic covariates, proves entrywise normality, and bootstraps simultaneous coefficient tests. It does not derive an extreme-value law for low-rank row factors or allow predictable masks.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Derive a uniform row-factor Bahadur representation and control covariance degeneracy before applying anti-concentration to the maximum over all rows.
seed_details.destination_search: Available simultaneous matrix results use multiplier calibration; no stable closed-form extreme-value limit was found when row-factor coordinates are strongly correlated.
seed_details.referee_objection: A multiplier theorem is sufficient, while a universal extreme-value limit fails under nearly collinear row scores.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is credible without a new correlation restriction, which would be dictated by the desired limit.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped to avoid imposing an artificial covariance condition merely to force a Gumbel law.

proposed_from.literature_map: Cai, Li, Chi, Poor, and Chen (2021, Annals of Statistics) give the closest independent-mask \(\ell_{2,\infty}\) spectral benchmark and a minimax noise obstruction, but their theorem contains independent-sampling terms not identical to \(b_{nm}\). Tropp (2011, Electronic Communications in Probability) supplies rectangular matrix Freedman concentration through Hermitian dilation and predictable quadratic variation, but not rowwise perturbation. Han, Sun, and Zhang (2025, Annals of Statistics) give online stochastic-gradient recovery and fixed-form doubly-debiased inference under adaptive matrix contexts. Khan and Ugander (2023, Journal of Causal Inference) derive optimal affine normalization under independent indicators and explicitly identify dependent indicators as future work. Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences) construct predictable weights and a scalar martingale central limit theorem for adaptive policy evaluation. Wang, Wong, Mao, and Chan (2021, International Conference on Machine Learning) pair balancing weights with a fixed heterogeneous-missingness Frobenius lower bound. Xia and Yuan (2021, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B) prove fixed-linear-form inference through debiasing and singular-space projection. Belloni and Oliveira (2018) provide high-dimensional martingale coupling and multiplier bootstrap for maxima. Ma, Niu, Zhang, and Zhu (2025, Journal of the American Statistical Association) provide matrix-specific pointwise and simultaneous inference under modeled nonadaptive missingness. Spruijt-Metz et al. (2022) document that HeartSteps II saved personalized decision probabilities, making recorded versus blind analysis a concrete design choice.

pre_d0_intent.topic: K1 prove IPW-SVD attains pointwise normalized max-row loss b_nm=K r^(3/2)mu q^(-1/2)sqrt(1/n+n/m^2) under recorded predictable masks. K2 match it by an adaptive-mask minimax lower bound. K3 prove blind row scaling is first-order valid iff restricted propensity drift rho<=b_nm. K4 keep b_nm separate and inflate simultaneous stochastic radii by sqrt(log |G_n|) for predeclared dense families |G_n|<=n^kappa. Include the rank-one .25/.75 Markov-mask witness and HeartSteps II consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Recorded propensities make IPW entry errors conditionally mean zero, so matrix Freedman concentration plus leave-one-row perturbation may recover the independent-mask rowwise scale. A constant-q subclass supplies a legal lower-bound packing. Expanding blind self-normalization should expose drift-correlated first-order bias. The Markov witness permits exact conditional calculations. Polynomial query families require a separate entropy multiplier; it cannot be hidden inside b_nm. Random denominator remainders and the iff threshold remain unchecked. A constant-propensity submodel also shows adaptivity cannot improve the minimax converse, but sharp constants remain open here. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Obtain martingale-sharp rowwise singular-vector perturbation, control adaptive self-normalized denominators, match the lower bound, and prove necessity and sufficiency of the drift threshold while separating simultaneous-query entropy. EARLY KILL TEST: Expand bias and variance exactly in the rank-one Markov witness. Stop if bias exceeds b_nm when rho<=b_nm, or if martingale concentration or sqrt(log |G_n|) inflation invalidates the stated pointwise benchmark.

banked_reason: The central theorem proves only c b_nm <= R*_nm <= C(1 wedge a_loose_nm); the fixed-complexity upper endpoint is nonshrinking, so the achieved tier is subfield below the field floor.
banked_proposal_promise_gap: The proposed matched b_nm IPW-SVD frontier is false on the frozen class. The banked result retains a sound b_nm-to-constant minimax bracket, estimator-specific IPW failure, d_nm blind resolution, Markov witness, and conservative simultaneous bands, but does not close the estimator-independent minimax rate.
